monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp drop in volume and intensity compared to last month, with significantly reduced run frequency, distance, and time spent in higher HR zones — suggesting either intentional recovery or emerging fatigue/availability constraints.
monthly_review.highlight: Zone 4 time dropped from 15% last month to just 1% this month — indicating a near-complete absence of threshold-level stimulus.

goal_tracker.message: You need 30.6 more km across 7 additional sessions in the remaining 26 days — averaging ~4.4 km per session, ideally spread over 3–4 runs/week to avoid overload.

insights.title: Stable efficiency despite pace decline
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency remained nearly identical (13.62 vs 13.66 km/hr per bpm) even as average pace slowed by 35 sec/km and avg HR dropped 12 bpm — suggesting preserved cardiovascular economy at lower intensities.

insights.title: Collapse in Zone 4+ training
insights.body: Zone 4 dropped from 15% to 1% and Zone 5 vanished entirely (4% → 0%), while Zone 1 dominance rose from 23% to 50% — indicating a strong shift toward very low-intensity recovery or deconditioning.

insights.title: Cadence-stride tradeoff evident in recent runs
insights.body: On 2026-04-29, cadence was 146 spm with stride length 88.65 cm and vertical oscillation 8.2 cm; on 2026-05-05, cadence rose to 144 spm but stride shrank to 68.33 cm — suggesting form instability or fatigue-induced shortening at similar effort levels.

insights.title: Low ground contact time consistency
insights.body: Ground contact time ranged from 301–327 ms across recent runs — tightly clustered and well below 330 ms (a common recreational benchmark), indicating maintained neuromuscular readiness despite reduced load.

recommendations.action: Do a 5 km Zone 2 run (HR 125–135 bpm) on Wednesday, focusing on holding cadence ≥140 spm and stride length ≥78 cm (per your 2026-05-02 baseline).
recommendations.reason: Your Zone 2 contribution is still solid (32% this month), but cadence dropped 4 spm overall — reinforcing rhythm at sustainable HR will rebuild efficiency without overstressing recovery.

recommendations.action: Add one 20-min Zone 3 interval session: 4 × 4 min @ HR 145–155 bpm, 90-sec walk recovery — keep pace between 510–530 sec/km (8:30–8:50 min/km).
recommendations.reason: Zone 3 is at 16% this month (down from 26%) and Zone 4 has nearly disappeared; reintroducing controlled threshold work will restore aerobic power without exceeding your current VO₂ max range (35–36).

recommendations.action: Perform a 3 km easy run on Saturday at Zone 1 HR ≤120 bpm, consciously reducing vertical oscillation target to ≤7.0 cm (your recent avg is 7.4 cm).
recommendations.reason: Vertical oscillation increased from 6.4 cm (2026-04-26) to 8.2 cm (2026-04-29) during faster efforts — lowering bounce at low intensity reinforces efficient posture and conserves energy for upcoming stimulus.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish rhythm, reinforce aerobic foundation, and gently reintroduce threshold stimulus — all while monitoring form metrics to ensure efficiency gains translate to sustainable pace.
